investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T12:50–12:57Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent never reached a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node available and no preemption victims eligible, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 130–144 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a runtime infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to only the two kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are full. If the affinity rules were broadened or corrected, the pod might schedule on other nodes — but only if those nodes also carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. This cannot be confirmed without inspecting the pod spec.

TERTIARY — transient cluster-level resource pressure: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads or other kata-class pods may have temporarily consumed all VM slots, causing a time-bounded exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity ceiling. The three evals ran sequentially over ~7 minutes and all failed, suggesting the condition persisted across the window rather than being a momentary spike.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes, which would shift the root cause from capacity exhaustion to a configuration regression.

A passing run of remote-agent-create on a different runtime environment or cluster that shares the same code — this would confirm the problem is environment-specific (cluster capacity) rather than a code or eval configuration defect.

Consider a separate eval for pod scheduling latency that fails fast (e.g., within 30s) when a pod remains Pending/Unschedulable, rather than waiting for the full outageLatencyMs timeout, to reduce mean time to detection for capacity events.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T12:52–12:57Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the required peer-pod VM because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes production cluster (6 nodes) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. This prevents any new remote-agent peer-pod from being scheduled. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers peer-pod VM provisioning; that provisioning stalls unscheduled for 130–144 seconds across all three checks before the eval times out. Because the agent is never created, the state-polling step that would produce orgId, agentId, readyState, and state evidence is never reached, causing a complete contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent peer-pod scheduling layer in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was returned by any check, meaning the agent pod never started and the runtime contract could not be exercised at all.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was left Unschedulable for 130–148 seconds before the eval timed out. Because no pod ever started, the agent was never created, no runtime response was produced, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool, not an application code defect and not a user-traffic incident (no traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T12:50–12:57Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent never reached a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node available and no preemption victims eligible, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 130–144 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a runtime infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to only the two kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are full. If the affinity rules were broadened or corrected, the pod might schedule on other nodes — but only if those nodes also carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. This cannot be confirmed without inspecting the pod spec.

TERTIARY — transient cluster-level resource pressure: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads or other kata-class pods may have temporarily consumed all VM slots, causing a time-bounded exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity ceiling. The three evals ran sequentially over ~7 minutes and all failed, suggesting the condition persisted across the window rather than being a momentary spike.
